newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian LSWR seen steady after Indonesian allocation.
newsitem.headline: Asian LSWR seen steady after Indonesian allocation.

text.p: The low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market in Asia is expected to be stable for March trading as supply is expected to balance demand, traders said on Friday.
"It is fairly balanced .. there is no particular push in either direction," said a trader with a major oil company.
The market sources said with market balanced they doubted Indonesia's supply to the spot market would cause any price ripples.

Indonesia, the region's main exporter of LSWR, earlier this week issued an export allocation of 3.7 million barrels, unchanged from February's initial allocation, but lower considering an additional 900,000 barrels were later supplied in February.
For March, traders expected state-owned Pertamina to make its usual additional allocation of around 500,000 to 600,000 barrels.

They said they doubted Pertamina rolled any February barrels into March allocation, but they said a U.S. refiner had offered to sell 600,000-barrels of end February LSWR, which could easily pressure March dates.

Traders said the March lifting programme had yet to be finalised but 1.9 million barrels were available from Platinum, 800,000 barrels from Balikpapan, 400,000 barrels each from Sungei Pakning and Sambu Jetti and 200,000 from Dumai.
They said supply from Dumai was slightly lower due to the the 38-day turnaround at the 120,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) refinery which is due to start this weekend.
"Dumai isn't a huge producer - usually 400,000 barrels a month -- it (the shutdown) has a neglible effect," said a trader.

The shutdown of the 83,000-bpd hydrocracker at 125,000-bpd Balongan refinery also would not add much surplus to the market as the topper throughput has been reduced, said a source close to the refinery.
"They would have to cut automatically if the hydrocracker is down," the source said.

Traders said they expected March barrels to maintain the current trading range of $20.00-$21.00 per barrel on a free-on-board basis Indonesia, or at a 40-to-70 cents premium range over Pertamina's selling formula, traders said.

Prices for February loading barrels fell nearly $3.00 per barrel, but did not fall below the $20.00 mark, a psychological support level, amid the extra supplies that emerged after the initial allocaton.
"I am quite surprised that with the extra in February, the market has held up so well, and has not been oversupplied," one trader said.
